title: Archway over La Silla
caption: The Milky Way arching over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way arches across the sky above ESO's La Silla Observatory in northern Chile. In the foreground rests the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope, SEST, while ESO's 3.6-metre telescope sits on a peak in the background.
SEST has been decommissioned, and ESO describes the slumbering dish as taking a moment to reflect on the cosmos overhead. Behind it, the 3.6-metre telescope keeps watch from its higher perch.

The arch overhead is our own galaxy seen edge-on from within. The Sun lies inside a flattened disc of stars, gas and dust, so when we look along that disc, the light of countless distant stars merges into a glowing band. Dark patches within it are clouds of dust that block the light from behind. Here that band arches over the observatory, framing the telescopes below.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way's arch appears brighter and more detailed here than in person.

explore: Submillimetre telescopes like SEST use dish antennas rather than glass mirrors, because they collect light at wavelengths longer than the eye can see. SEST no longer observes, but still points upward.
alt: The Milky Way arching across the night sky above a retired telescope, with another telescope on a peak in the background.
